title: Implement software solutions that meet regulatory compliance requirements
description: Identify relevant regulatory frameworks applicable to software systems, apply compliance requirements during development and testing phases, and document compliance evidence for audit purposes. Students will demonstrate this by analyzing regulatory requirements for a given domain and implementing corresponding controls in a software project.
soft_skills_description: Careful analysis of complex regulatory documents and precise implementation of requirements demand strong attention to detail and systematic analytical capabilities.
rationale: The title directly incorporates the core action 'ensure' from the source skills while expanding it to the software engineering context. This competency combines both knowledge elements ('compliance', 'regulatory compliance') with the practical skill ('ensure regulatory compliance') into a unified learning outcome. Learners prove mastery by showing they can translate abstract compliance requirements into concrete technical implementations, such as data protection measures or audit trails. This competency stands alone because it addresses the complete workflow from understanding regulations to implementing compliant solutions, distinct from general software quality or security topics.
future_relevance: Stable - Regulatory requirements continue to expand across industries (GDPR, HIPAA, PCI-DSS, etc.) making compliance skills increasingly essential for software professionals.

title: Integrate and secure application programming interfaces (APIs) in software systems
description: Connect software applications and services by implementing and consuming RESTful APIs with proper authentication, authorization mechanisms. Apply security best practices to protect API endpoints from common vulnerabilities. Utilize API management platforms to monitor, version, and maintain API lifecycles within distributed systems.
soft_skills_description: Understanding system dependencies and data flow; designing robust integration points; documenting API contracts for other developers.
rationale: API integration is a central and recurring theme across the skills, explicitly mentioned in multiple items. This competency focuses on the practical ability to work with APIs—a fundamental skill for modern software integration. It combines the technical act of integration (REST) with the crucial security layer (cybersecurity, authentication) and operational aspects (observability, platform management). The supporting technical skills show the context of where API work happens. Length: 380 chars.
future_relevance: Growing - APIs are the backbone of modern software architecture, and their secure management is increasingly critical with microservices এবং cloud-native designs.

title: Containerize applications and manage deployments using container orchestration
description: Package software applications into Docker containers and deploy them to Kubernetes clusters for scalable, resilient operations. Configure container images, manage container lifecycles, and implement basic deployment strategies.
soft_skills_description: Methodical approach to configuration and deployment processes with careful attention to environment variables, networking, and security settings
rationale: Docker and Kubernetes represent the complete container workflow from packaging to orchestration. Learners demonstrate mastery by creating Dockerfiles for applications, building and pushing container images to registries, and deploying those containers to Kubernetes clusters with appropriate configurations. This competency focuses on the operational lifecycle of containerized applications, distinguishing it from infrastructure provisioning. The skills are complementary as containers require orchestration for production use, making this a natural learning progression from packaging to deployment management.
future_relevance: Stable, as containerization has become the standard deployment model for cloud-native applications with continued adoption across industries.

title: Provision infrastructure using infrastructure-as-code and manage version control
description: Define and deploy cloud infrastructure using Terraform configuration files and maintain code repositories with Git version control. Implement declarative infrastructure definitions, manage state files, and follow branching strategies for collaborative development.
soft_skills_description: Ability to work in teams using shared repositories and maintain clear documentation for infrastructure configurations and change histories
rationale: Terraform and Git represent modern infrastructure and code management practices. Mastery is demonstrated by writing Terraform modules to provision cloud resources, managing infrastructure state, and using Git for version control with proper branching and merging workflows. This competency focuses on declarative infrastructure definition and collaborative development practices, distinct from container operations. The pairing is logical as infrastructure code requires version control, and both skills support reproducible, auditable infrastructure management essential for DevOps practices.
future_relevance: Emerging, as infrastructure-as-code adoption accelerates with cloud migration and Git remains foundational for all software development workflows.
